metadata.title: Symmetry Transition Preserving Chirality in QCD: A Versatile Random Matrix Model

extraction_notes.note: The paper (PRL format) is organised by run-in \paragraph headings that latex_facts.py does not report as sections, so every node carries an empty section field.

Derivations run into the displayed results mid-sentence ('...yielding \begin{equation}'), so the prose proof nodes end at the last whole sentence before the sentence carrying the result; EP8 (superbosonized partition function) has no proof node since its justification is the same sentence that contains EP7, and is linked by uses edges instead.

Numbered equations retyped as claims (equation was the alternative): the text calls eq. (10) 'the result' and eq. (14) 'a new result', and each is the conclusion of a prose derivation, which needs a result as proves target; rigor semi_formal since the derivations omit steps deferred to a companion paper.
Numbered equation retyped as an external theorem because the text introduces it as a cited Bessel-function identity (Abramowitz-Stegun 9.6.1).
The conjecture spans two sentences: the stated conjecture and the following sentence that ties it to this model's chirality-preserving transition.

Physics background in the introduction (dimensional reduction at high temperature, chiral restoration, applications to graphene and condensed matter), the abstract, the figure caption and the bibliography footnote on counting four-component fermions were not extracted as nodes.

nodes.statement: In the large-N limit the saddle point equation~ still applies though with a different dimension in the unit matrix. For this reason we use the parametrization U'_bb& = Le^-vartheta_1tau_3/2e^-vartheta_2tau_2/2tau_1e^z_11_2+z_2 tau_1e^vartheta_2tau_2/2e^vartheta_1tau_3/2,\\ U'_ff& = e^-ivarphi_1tau_3/2e^-ivarphi_2tau_2/2tau_1e^i(z_31_2+z_4 tau_1)e^ivarphi_2tau_2/2e^ivarphi_1tau_3/2, for the two diagonal blocks of U'. The angles take the values z_1,z_2,vartheta_1,vartheta_2inR, varphi_1in[-pi,pi], and varphi_2,z_3,z_4in[-pi/2,pi/2]. From the saddle point equation and the properties of U'_bb and U'_ff we have to expand the variables z_j as follows: (z_1,z_2)=(delta z_1/sqrtN,delta z_2/sqrtN) and (z_3,z_4)=(delta z_3/sqrtN, delta z_4/sqrtN), ~(z_3,z_4)=(pi/2+delta z_3/sqrtN,pi/2+delta z_4/sqrtN). The latter expansion for z_3,z_4 yields an algebraically 1/N-suppressed term. The expansion to leading order in 1/N and integration over eta and delta z_j is quite lengthy and we omit it here. It is done in detail in. Afterwards we integrate over varphi_1 and vartheta_1 which yields the modified Bessel functions of first order, I_j, and of second order, K_j, respectively.

nodes.statement: In we have shown that the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all k-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix D are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions.
conclusions: In we have shown that the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all k-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix D are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions.
